name: real-skills
description: Everyday engineering skills: changelog (release notes from promotion PRs or tags, linked to your tracker), quick-ask-me (short interview that ends in an implementation brief) ask-and-create-specs (interview that ends in a terse, line-capped spec), create-spec (sizes the work, asks at most one round, writes a terse spec other skills hand off to), create-plan (spec to an ordered task plan checked by a script), wtf (read-only bug-report triage with a checked verdict), wtf-and-create-ticket (wtf, then one ticket with the triage, cause, fix and plan), solve-merge-conflicts (makes a conflicted pull request mergeable again, with checked resolutions and one push after a yes), fix-ci (makes a pull request's red checks green: failures classed, the fix proven by the failing command, one push after a yes), clean-slop (removes the slop a branch added under the repo's checks, one local commit), review-prs (pull-request review with checked findings), qa-this (QA off production with recorded results, evidence comments and a report), check-infra-and-migrations (is this PR or promotion safe to push: migrations, infrastructure, a verdict and a runbook), promote (one environment to the next through a gated pull request, with two approvals, watch and verify), calibrate (switches on logged Jev questions once they have earned it) and handoff-with-prompt (writes a handoff file and prints a prompt for the next agent). do-shit is Claude Code only.

interface.shortDescription: Changelogs, planning interviews, terse specs, bug-report triage, PR review, QA, release safety checks and gated promotions
